# frame — full usage

The complete output of `frame --help`, kept current by CI.

```text
frame - an AI harness built on: zsh, ghostty, neovim, and claude code

A frame is a terminal window running neovim as its buffer-management layer —
running Claude with supporting service buffers and a terminal (local).

Usage:

    frame init [--type T…]            scaffold .frame/ into a project
    frame init --types                list the project types

    frame wt TOPIC                    create/reuse branch + worktree, boot it
    frame wt TOPIC --from SRC_FRAME   …and resume SRC_FRAME's warm claude
                                      session in it (carry context across
                                      topics). If SRC_FRAME's claude is live,
                                      it's asked to wrap up and retire itself.
                                      SRC_FRAME: a topic, or NAME/TOPIC for
                                      another project (the :FrameName form)
    frame wt TOPIC --resume ID        …resume a raw session id instead
    frame wt                          boot the worktree you're already in
    frame wt -d [-f] [TOPIC]          tear down a frame (default: current)

    frame shell TOPIC                 minimal frame in the current dir — no
                                      branch, just the claude + local buffers;
                                      nothing is written into the dir (refuses ~)
    frame shell -C DIR TOPIC          …in DIR instead (either form opens the
                                      dir's .frame/config.sh BUFFERS, if any)
    frame shell [TOPIC] --find "WORDS" [-g]
                                      find a past claude session by what YOU
                                      typed in it (every word; tool output and
                                      replies don't count), pick one, resume it
    frame shell [TOPIC] --recent [-g]
                                      browse your most recent sessions (first
                                      message of each) and resume the one you pick.
                                      Both lists cover the repo you're in: its
                                      main checkout and its worktrees, live or
                                      torn down (outside a repo, or -g: every
                                      session). ● marks one open now — picking
                                      it switches to it
    frame shell [TOPIC] --resume ID   …resume a known session id in the dir
                                      it ran in (-C DIR: in DIR instead). A
                                      torn-down frame wt worktree resumes in the
                                      main checkout; a live one reboots its frame.
                                      Resuming, TOPIC defaults to the dir's
                                      name (-2, -3… if a live frame has it)
    frame shell -d [TOPIC]            tear down a shell frame (default: current)
                                      — just quits the session; the dir is kept

    frame stop [TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC|--all] [-f]
                                      shut a frame down gracefully and keep it
                                      restorable: Ctrl-C its terminal buffers,
                                      wait for them to exit, quit nvim. Refuses
                                      on unsaved buffers (-f overrides)
    frame restore [TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC|--all] [--print]
                                      reboot frames that went down without a
                                      teardown (crash, reboot, Ghostty quit,
                                      frame stop), each in its own tab, claude
                                      resumed and told to wait for you. Bare
                                      form lists them and asks which
    frame restore --forget TOPIC|--all
                                      drop a frame's record instead

    frame spawn shell TOPIC [--req TEXT] [--timeout N] [--ephemeral]
                                      boot a shell frame into a tab group

    frame spawn wt TOPIC [--cwd PATH] [--req TEXT] [--timeout N]
                         [--from SRC_FRAME | --resume ID]
                                      boot a worktree frame into a tab group;
                                      --from/--resume carry a warm claude
                                      session in (see frame wt)

    frame ls                          list frames

    frame view [TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC]     dump one frame's full state (default:
                                      the frame you're in), incl. its kv
                                      settings off their default + notes

    frame merge [TOPIC] [--push|--no-push|--ff|-n]
                                      merge TOPIC into the primary branch
                                      (default: current branch); pushes
                                      when push_on_merge is on (see frame kv)

    frame push [-n]                   push the primary branch to origin — the
                                      follow-up to a bare frame merge. The
                                      primary branch is whatever the primary
                                      checkout is on (main, master, …)

    frame claude [--timeout N] TEXT…  talk to THIS frame's own claude: type
                                      TEXT into it and block until it answers,
                                      then print the answer

    frame req TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC TEXT…  send a request to ANOTHER frame's Claude
                                      (types TEXT into its prompt); arms a
                                      one-shot reply to your inbox

    frame req status [TOKEN…]         what became of requests you sent and
                                      haven't read the reply to: queued #N,
                                      working, blocked, in your inbox, lost

    frame inbox [--wait [--timeout N] [--count K | --for TOKEN…]]
                                      show + clear this frame's inbox;
                                      --wait blocks until a message arrives;
                                      --for exits 5 if a reply is lost

    frame reply [TEXT…]               frames use to reply to last req

    frame deliver TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC TEXT…
                                      send a message to a frame's inbox

    frame status [TEXT…]              append "- TEXT" to this frame's window
                                      title (no TEXT restores the base title)

    frame name                        print this frame's NAME/TOPIC to stdout —
                                      the handle for frame req/focus/view

    frame focus [TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC]    raise that frame's ghostty window
                                      (default: the frame you're in)

    frame notify                      set title to "waiting" + fire the
                                      task-complete banner

    frame services [up|down]          manage the shared postgres/minio stack

    frame notifications on|off|init   on|off: global switch;
                                      init: build/repair the banner icon

    frame silence [--off] [TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC]
                                      silence one frame's banners (--off
                                      restores; default: the frame you're
                                      in) — the CLI twin of :FrameSilence

    frame yolo on|off                 master switch: claude in every frame
                                      launches --dangerously-skip-permissions
                                      (default off; bare form shows the state)

    frame kv                          settings telling each frame's claude how
                                      far to go on its own: autocommit,
                                      merge_on_commit, push_on_merge,
                                      deploy_on_merge (default false),
                                      spawn_frames (default true).
                                      Bare form lists values + source layer
    frame kv get KEY                  print KEY's effective value
    frame kv set [--project|--user] KEY VALUE
                                      set KEY for this frame (default), every
                                      frame of the project, or every project
    frame kv unset [--project|--user] KEY
                                      drop KEY from that layer
    frame kv describe [KEY]           what KEY means: type, default, where
                                      declared. Declare your own keys in
                                      .frame/kv.defaults (project, committed)
                                      or ~/.config/frame/kv.defaults (user).
                                      Undeclared keys are the agent's own
                                      notes, on its frame only
    frame kv --of TOPIC|NAME/TOPIC [get KEY | describe [KEY]]
                                      read another live frame's kv (read-only)

    frame swarm [off|1|2]             how much each frame's claude is told
                                      at session start about being a frame:
                                      0 off · 1 aware (identity + safe-action
                                      rules) · 2 ask (+ query siblings), the
                                      current ceiling (3 reserved, not built)
                                      (default off; bare form shows the level)

Example:
    cd $YOUR_GIT_REPO && frame init
    frame wt TOPIC
```
